title: Performance regression validation + acceptance gates for TP stability fixes (runtime-1.19)
creator: Sofia Ivanova
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Goal
Validate that the TP hang/stability fixes (scheduler lifecycle changes, collective async-error handling, watchdog/quarantine, instrumentation) do NOT introduce material performance regressions (throughput, latency, tail behavior) in key production-like workloads.

This issue defines:
- Benchmark suite updates needed to cover the new failure-handling paths (watchdog/quarantine, async error checks)
- Acceptance gates for runtime-1.19 promotion (Hosted canary -> wider Hosted -> Dedicated opt-in)
- What to measure and how to interpret changes under mixed-length and streaming-heavy traffic

Why this is P0
We are changing hot paths around collectives + scheduling. Even small sync points or too-aggressive watchdog polling can show up as:
- Increased TTFT for chat/streaming
- Reduced tokens/sec at high concurrency
- Higher tail latencies due to fairness/backpressure changes

Scope
In-scope
- Perf baselines + A/B comparison between runtime-1.18.x and runtime-1.19-rc* on identical hardware/software.
- Add/adjust benchmark-lab scenarios to cover: long streaming, mixed seq lengths, cancellation churn, overload patterns.
- Define promotion gates for Hosted canary and Dedicated opt-in.

Out-of-scope
- New model onboarding perf work (unless a regression only reproduces on a specific model).

Test matrix (minimum)
Hardware targets (Hosted-like + Dedicated-like):
- H100 SXM (8x) TP=8, DP=1 (primary)
- A100 80GB (8x) TP=8, DP=1 (secondary)

Models/workloads (representative)
1) Chat streaming (long-running)
- Prompt: 1–4k input tokens
- Output: 1–4k streamed tokens
- Concurrency: 64 / 128
- Cancellation churn: 2% / 5% disconnect mid-stream (forced)

2) Mixed sequence lengths (fairness stress)
- 70% short (<=256 out), 30% long (>=2k out)
- Concurrency: 128

3) Overload/backpressure scenario
- Ramp to saturation; verify we degrade gracefully (queueing + shedding) rather than tanking GPU efficiency.

4) “Healthy fast path” microbench
- No cancels, no injected delays, steady-state batching; ensures watchdog polling/async error checks are not adding measurable overhead.

Metrics to compare (record P50/P95/P99 where relevant)
Primary
- Throughput: output tokens/sec per TP group and per GPU
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) for streaming
- TP95/TP99 end-to-end latency for non-stream requests
- GPU utilization and kernel time breakdown (as available via existing profiler hooks)

Secondary / guardrails
- Rate of watchdog triggers (should be ~0 in healthy run)
- Number of TP-group quarantines/resets
- Collective latency histograms (p95/p99) and variance
- Scheduler queue depth / starvation counters

Acceptance gates (promotion criteria)
Hosted canary promotion gate (runtime-1.19)
- Throughput regression <= 1.5% at steady-state vs 1.18.x (H100 primary workload #1 + #2)
- TTFT regression <= 2.0% at p95 (workload #1)
- p99 latency regression <= 3.0% for non-stream (workload #2)
- No increase in error rate in canary attributable to the changes (timeouts/5xx) beyond normal noise; watchdog triggers in healthy scenarios <= 0.01% of requests

Dedicated opt-in gate
- Same thresholds as Hosted plus:
- Stability under 4-hour soak at high concurrency with cancels enabled (workload #1) and no progressive drift (tokens/sec stable within 2% over time)

Implementation plan
1) Benchmark suite updates
- Coordinate with Sahana Iyer on perf-canary workflow (nightly TP overload tests + stall detection artifacts).
- Ensure benchmark-lab includes new scenario definitions from PR-911 and can run A/B on two runtime images.

2) Baselines
- Pin driver + NCCL versions and record in artifacts.
- Baseline runtime-1.18.x on H100 + A100 for workloads #1-#4.

3) Run candidates
- Test runtime-1.19-rc1 with watchdog enabled (default planned for Hosted canary).
- Also run with watchdog disabled (flag) to isolate overhead if regression appears.

4) Report + sign-off
- One-page perf summary with links to artifacts and dashboards.
- Get runtime leads (Sofia/Hiro) + SRE (Rafael) sign-off before broader canary ramp.

Open questions
- What is the default watchdog polling interval in Hosted (see PR-18473)? Need to ensure it isn’t too aggressive for high-throughput steady-state.
- Do we need a separate gate for "many small requests" (embedding-like) under TP? (My hunch: no, but confirm with SRE incident patterns.)
comments: 2025-02-18 (Marcus Reed): Drafted the benchmark matrix above. Biggest risk is watchdog polling + async error checks adding a tiny but persistent sync overhead. I’ll run A/B with watchdog disabled to quantify pure overhead vs functional changes.

2025-02-19 (Sahana Iyer): Perf-canary PR-288 is ready for review; it runs the new TP overload suite nightly and archives stall-detection artifacts. Once merged, we can use it as a gating signal for canary ramp.
2025-02-20 (Isabella Rossi): I can cover microbench (#4) on H100 to isolate kernel-level regressions. Will post tokens/sec + kernel timeline diffs between 1.18.x and 1.19-rc1.

2025-02-22 (Marcus Reed): Baseline results (runtime-1.18.6) collected on H100 8x: workload #1 tokens/sec stable; TTFT p95 recorded. Artifacts linked in benchmark-lab run history (internal). Next up: rc1.

2025-02-24 (Marcus Reed): Initial rc1 run shows ~2.3% throughput drop in workload #2 (mixed lengths). TTFT within noise. Suspect scheduler fairness change interacting with watchdog progress accounting (more frequent progress updates => contention). Filed a follow-up note to Sofia; will retest with progress counters sampling reduced (if safe).

2025-02-25 (Sofia Ivanova): Confirmed the progress counter update frequency is configurable; we can lower sampling rate without losing stuck detection resolution. Please rerun rc1 with sampling at 250ms vs 50ms and compare.

2025-02-26 (Marcus Reed): Rerun with progress sampling at 250ms: throughput regression improved to 0.8% (within gate). No missed detections in injected-stall tests (workload #3). Proposing 250ms as Hosted default; Dedicated can tune if needed.

2025-02-27 (Rafael Mendes): From SRE POV, gates look good. Please add a 4-hour soak run with cancels enabled before we sign off Dedicated opt-in. Also confirm watchdog triggers remain near-zero in healthy runs; we’ll alert on any spike during canary.

2025-03-02 (Marcus Reed): 4-hour soak completed (H100, workload #1 cancels 5%): tokens/sec drift <1.2%, TTFT stable, watchdog triggers 0, quarantines 0. Injected-stall run still triggers watchdog as expected and recovers (quarantine+teardown).

2025-03-04 (Marcus Reed): Final perf summary posted to internal notes: all acceptance gates passed on H100; A100 secondary shows throughput regression 1.1% (within gate). Requesting sign-off to close ENG-2409 and proceed with canary ramp per rollout checklist.
2025-03-05 (Rafael Mendes): Signed off. Please ensure dashboards (ENG-2408) include the regression panels + link this ticket from the runtime-1.19 go/no-go thread. Marking Done.
